title: Diagnosed with ADHD as an adult: next steps
dek: Put follow-ups, clinic contacts, prescription questions, and records requests in one place. Separate necessary admin from optional disclosure.
metaDescription: Put follow-ups, clinic contacts, prescription questions, and records requests in one place. Separate necessary admin from optional disclosure.

paragraphs: After an adult ADHD diagnosis, confirm the next appointment, who coordinates your care, and how to contact the team between visits. If medication is prescribed, ask the prescriber and pharmacy for your specific prescription and supply process. Put these answers on one page; you do not need to redesign your entire life or make every disclosure decision immediately.

A diagnosis can arrive with relief, questions, or both. It can also arrive with a portal message, a referral, and three unanswered calls. This guide addresses that paperwork and follow-through, not which treatment to choose or how to change a prescribed medicine.

body.heading: Before the next appointment
items: Save the assessment report or ask how to obtain it.
Confirm the name and contact details of the clinician responsible for follow-up.
Write the next appointment date, booking status, and what to bring.
Ask what to do about questions or problems between visits.
If prescribed medication, get the prescription and supply process in writing.
Confirm who sends records to primary care and whether consent is needed.
Put requested forms and actual deadlines on the page.
Choose one existing admin problem to support, not a whole-system overhaul.

body.heading: Make a care-contact page, not a second medical chart
paragraphs: Keep clinic contact details, appointment logistics, the report's location, and questions you need answered. Store diagnosis and prescription information privately. A general household task board does not need your full assessment report.

[NIMH's adult ADHD information](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/adhd-what-you-need-to-know) explains that adults can be diagnosed and that assessment looks beyond a single current difficulty. Once diagnosed, your practical task is to understand the plan agreed with your provider. You do not have to re-prove the diagnosis to every person helping with an appointment.

body.heading: Invented example: a follow-up page
rows: November 30 at 10:00; booked, not just requested
Bring questions and the information the clinic specifically requested
Verified clinic number and secure-message route
Await written answer from prescriber; do not assume automatic repeats
Ask whether report reached primary care
Call clinic to confirm who handles between-visit questions

body.heading: Ask how this prescription process actually works
paragraphs: Rules and workflows differ by medicine, country, clinician, insurer, and pharmacy. Ask whether a new prescription, appointment, authorization, or other step is required and who initiates it. Ask how far ahead to request the next supply, then use that answer rather than a generic reminder interval.

If a pharmacy cannot supply what was prescribed, contact the pharmacist and prescriber for the appropriate next step. Do not change dose, borrow medication, substitute a product, or stop treatment based on an organizing article. Keep the contact attempt and response date so you can follow up without rebuilding the story.

body.heading: Questions to read from your page

items.line: Who is responsible for my follow-up and prescription requests, and how do I reach them?
What should I do if I have a treatment concern before the next appointment, and which contact route should I use?
The pharmacy cannot supply my prescription. Please tell me the appropriate next step and who needs to coordinate it.
Has my assessment report been sent to [provider], and what consent or request is still needed?
What appointments, authorizations, or charges should I expect, and who can confirm my coverage?

body.heading: Build reminders around actions, not just appointments
paragraphs: A reminder at the appointment time does not help you arrange transport or complete a requested form. Add a preparation action and a departure time where useful. Keep the booking acknowledgment so a request does not become an appointment in your head before it is confirmed.

For repeated administration, set a review date based on the actual office process. Check that someone has accepted a handoff before assuming responsibility transferred. This matters when moving between private and public care, clinicians, or insurers. A referral sent and a referral accepted are different states.

body.heading: Separate disclosure choices from required questions
paragraphs: Telling friends or an employer is a different question from completing a particular insurance, licensing, or benefits form accurately. Do not assume a universal duty to disclose, or a universal absence of one. Read the question and the relevant current local guidance, and seek appropriate advice where the consequences matter.

If you want workplace adjustments, ask the relevant workplace contact about its process and what documentation is needed. Share only what is appropriate for that purpose. This guide does not decide legal eligibility, confidentiality protections, or what an employer must provide.

body.heading: Support one live difficulty
paragraphs: Choose the admin problem costing you most right now: missed bills, appointment preparation, unopened letters, or starting a form. Give it a specific support, such as a funding-account check, an appointment page, or company while opening the envelope. A diagnosis does not clear a backlog automatically.

[Executive function and procrastination](/guides/executive-dysfunction-is-not-procrastination) can help describe a task barrier without treating every problem as the same. Keep medical questions for your clinician, and use the practical record to avoid losing agreed next steps.

body.heading: When to contact someone sooner
paragraphs: Do not wait for the routine review if you are unsure how to follow the treatment plan, cannot access prescribed care, or have a new concern. Ask the care team or pharmacist through the route they specified. For urgent or severe symptoms, use urgent medical services rather than waiting for an administrative reply.

[NICE's ADHD guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng87/chapter/Recommendations) addresses clinical follow-up and monitoring. It is not a reason to impose one appointment schedule on everyone. Write down the schedule and escalation instructions actually agreed for you.

items.q: What should I do first after diagnosis?
items.a: Confirm the care plan and the next follow-up with the clinician, then record the responsible contact and any preparation required. If a prescription is involved, ask about its specific process. Optional purchases, new planners, and broad disclosure decisions do not have to be your first jobs.

items.q: How early should I request a repeat prescription?
items.a: Ask your prescriber and pharmacist for the process and lead time that apply to your medicine and location. There is no universal interval this guide can give. Put the confirmed action date in your calendar and check that a request was received.

That decision depends on your goals, circumstances, and local rules. If seeking adjustments, ask about the formal process and documentation before sharing a full report. Obtain qualified advice for a consequential legal or employment question rather than relying on a general admin guide.

sources.name: NIMH: ADHD in adults
sources.note: Adults can receive an ADHD diagnosis; assessment considers earlier history, and treatment decisions belong with qualified providers.

sources.name: NICE: ADHD recommendations
sources.note: Clinical guidance supports planned follow-up and monitoring; it does not establish one refill or access process for every patient or jurisdiction.
